newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls after Bank Negara lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls after Bank Negara lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell on Monday after Bank Negara Malaysia came in to lend one-month funds in the morning, dealers said.
They said the overnight dropped to 7.5 percent from 8.2 before rebounding back to 7.8 percent at the close.
"Bank Negara was lending direct to banks this morning, and this shows how serious they are to bring rates lower," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
In the morning, interbank rates also fell after the central bank imposed curbs on foreign exchange swaps in an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit.
One-week money was at 7.5/8.5 percent against 8.7/8 percent on Friday.
One-month money was at 8.3 percent from 8.6/7 percent, and three-month was at 8.0/3 percent against 8.3/5 percent.
Bank Negara announced on Sunday that local banks would have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer, from Monday.
It said the move was to help control interest rates more effectively. The central bank has in the last two weeks been trying to lower interest rates in an effort to boost domestic economic activity.
On Friday, Bank Negara had asked banks to hold their base lending rates steady despite the recent surge in interbank rates.
"The market perception is that rates are heading lower," said one dealer.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were sharply up across the board to reflect softening in interbank rates, futures market dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up 18 points to 92.40, or an implied yield of 7.60 percent.
The December contract rose 14 to 92.64, or 7.36 percent while March 1998 was up 13 to 92.73, or 7.27 percent.
